verdict.rationale: Honeybadger documents deployment tracking that records deploys with revisions, says it can "correlate code changes with errors", links each revision to a GitHub/GitLab diff of what changed since the last deploy, and supports searching errors that occurred after the last deploy. There is no evidence that each issue shows the release it first appeared in, or that Honeybadger identifies a suspect commit for an issue. Missing for 10: per-issue first-seen release display, suspect-commit identification, independent corroboration of release-to-error correlation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can associate errors with releases and commits so each issue shows the release it first appeared in and the suspect commit that likely caused it

citations.quote: Deployment tracking lets you record when your app is deployed, see a history of deployments, and correlate code changes with errors.
When GitHub or GitLab is connected, Honeybadger links the revision to a comparison page that shows a diff of what changed since the last deploy.
Errors that occurred since the most recent deployment
Use this endpoint to notify Honeybadger when a deploy occurs.
